rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's eighteen builder trees go (eleven corals, ficus, jacarandas, a magnolia, canary date and queen palms); seven come back on their own spots, one for about every two houses, spread over the back yards, each 3 m or more from the nearest fence and 5 m or more from a wall. The palms 1.2 and 4.7 m from walls stay out.

trees.why: the back yard of the Spanish house on the north row: shade over the kettle grill where the family cooks
the tudor's back yard, behind the adirondack chair: a magnolia to sit under
the back lot line between the two north-row yards, 3 m off the stucco wall: a coral tree that shades both yards
the back yard of a south-row house, 12 m from its wall: the yard's one tree
the west corner lot's yard by the adirondack chair: shade for whoever sits there
the open back lawn of the southern row, far from the walls (24 m): a full-sized coral tree in the middle of the lot corner
the back yard on the east of the southern row: an old ficus, 7.5 m from the house
